excerpt: Fine’s (1994) notion of essence is primitive, and he uses the notion of a ‘real’ as opposed to ‘nominal’ definition to communicate the notion he has mind. The basic idea is that, while a nominal definition says what a term means, a real definition tells us what an entity is. ... If p is an essential truth with respect to entity e, then p is true regardless of what the world might be like; the truth of p doesn’t turn on how things turn out. Cast in terms of grounding, the idea is that the essential truths lack worldly grounds.
overview: This evidence explains why essential truths can underwrite metaphysical necessity in the main argument. By adopting Fine’s real-definition conception, the paper treats essential truths as not depending on contingent worldly arrangements. That makes the transition from an essential truth of the form ∧D → p to □(∧D → p) intelligible.
title: Finean Essence Necessity
